decision: Does the substring test for delete/remove operator names misclassify branch conflicts, and can conflict typing be derived entirely from exact effects and declarations?
hypothesis: An effect-derived conflict typing will eliminate false DELETE_MODIFY conflicts (and catch missed ones) without changing merge legality.
implementation_status: landed_on_main_via_pr_965 (commit 5e182534); this iter re-verifies the acceptance criteria at HEAD and refreshes the audit evidence stamp

before_after.classifier_before: substring test (`"remove" in value or "delete" in value`) over operator IDs (merge.py _conflict_kind, pinned baseline 5cd5b8b)
before_after.classifier_after: classify_merge_effects over AstOperatorV1 declarations, ActionEffectV1 exact effects (explicit consumed/produced NodeRef flow), and base-reference lineage; no operator-ID inspection

operators: openui.relocate (balanced consumed+produced node flow, move semantics)
regression_cases.name_heuristic_label: delete_modify (FALSE POSITIVE: name matches, no node is removed)

regression_cases.case: removal semantics without delete/remove in the name
operators: openui.rename_again (property delta on the same target)
regression_cases.effect_derived_label: delete_modify with the exact target fingerprint

regression_cases.case: unproven removal (topology delta without explicit node flow)
regression_cases.name_heuristic_label: delete_modify only if the name matched; otherwise silently classified by category
regression_cases.effect_derived_label: unsupported_effect (conservative typed refusal, target fingerprint attached)

registered_pair_audit.note: On the registered OpenUI local/topology corpus both labelings agree; the name heuristic's misclassifications are proven at the metamorphic unit level (misleading names, renamed declarations), which the fixed registered corpus does not contain.

acceptance_criteria.no_production_classifier_on_name_substri: pass (grep over src/slm_training/dsl/operators finds no operator-name substring test; the heuristic survives only as the labeled `_historical_label` audit baseline in scripts/audit_merge_conflicts.py)
acceptance_criteria.merge_replays_through_pack_authority: pass (merge_conversation_branches replays each edit via library.replay before classification; replay mismatch is a typed UNSUPPORTED_EFFECT refusal)
acceptance_criteria.incomplete_effects_fail_conservatively: pass (non-EXACT coverage, empty refs, declaration/effect-signature mismatch, or unproven removal all return UNSUPPORTED_EFFECT)
acceptance_criteria.stale_ref_priority: pass (STALE_REF is returned before overlap classification in both merge_conversation_branches and classify_merge_effects)

tests.neighboring: pytest -q tests/test_dsl/ -k 'operator or merge or transaction or topology or local': 244 passed

caveats: Fixture/wiring evidence only; no model, training, or ship claim.

Registered-corpus audit shows zero old/new disagreements, so the measured production impact on the current OpenUI corpus is nil; the fix removes name-dependent semantics and is proven on adversarial metamorphic fixtures, not on a registered-pair flip.
Historical DELETE_MODIFY name labels are retained in scripts/audit_merge_conflicts.py solely as a comparison baseline; production merge code never calls it.
